message: Can you read this ECG for me?
reply:
My reading from this image is **sinus rhythm at about 65 beats/minute, with no obvious major rhythm or conduction abnormality.**

- **Rhythm:** Regular, with a P wave before each heartbeat.
- **Axis and intervals:** Appear within normal limits; the QRS complexes are narrow.
- **ST segments/T waves:** Mild upward ST changes in the front chest leads, particularly V2–V3, may reflect a normal repolarization variant. I don’t see a clear acute heart attack pattern, but a single ECG image cannot rule one out.

Overall, this looks **largely reassuring**, subject to your symptoms and comparison with any previous ECG. Measurements from an image are approximate.

What is your age, why was the ECG taken, and are you having any symptoms? **If you currently have chest pain, shortness of breath, fainting, or cold sweats, seek emergency care now**, regardless of this reading.

[Reference: ECG interpretation and normal intervals](https://www.merckmanuals.com/professional/cardiovascular-disorders/cardiovascular-tests-and-procedures/electrocardiography?ruleredirectid=747)
